title: Why Festus Thought Paul Was Insane
paragraphs: Why Festus Thought Paul Was Insane
There are moments in Scripture that feel so painfully human that you can almost hear the room breathing.
Acts 26 is one of those moments.

A chained apostle stands before governors, military commanders, political elites, intellectuals, religious authorities, and a king. The air is heavy with suspicion. Roman authority watches carefully. Jewish accusers burn with hatred. Pride fills the hall like smoke.
And then Paul starts talking about resurrection.
A dead man who walked out of His grave.
A crucified Messiah who was alive.
And suddenly the governor Festus cannot contain himself anymore.
"Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad." — Acts 26:24 (KJV)
The Greek text is even sharper.
The Greek word μαίνῃ (mainē) comes from μαίνομαι (mainomai), meaning:
• to rage • to be out of one’s mind • to be mentally deranged • to speak as someone overtaken by madness
He was declaring that Paul had crossed the line between intelligence and insanity.
To the Roman mind… Paul sounded completely impossible.
Because the Gospel has always sounded irrational to people who worship power, image, control, status, logic without God, and earthly systems.
The tragedy is that many people still react to Jesus exactly like Festus did.
Some people hear the Gospel and feel conviction.
Others hear the Gospel and think believers have lost their minds.
Because resurrection destroys the illusion that this world is all there is.
And people become very uncomfortable when eternity interrupts their reality.
He could handle religion as long as it remained manageable.
But he could not process a man who stood before possible execution with supernatural peace while boldly declaring that death itself had already been defeated.
But it did not understand surrender.
But it did not understand grace.
Rome understood gods made by men.
But it did not understand a God who became flesh and died for sinners.
And maybe that is why this moment still cuts so deeply today.
Because modern culture still celebrates confidence but mocks holiness.
People will believe crystals carry energy.
They will believe the universe sends signs.
They will believe strangers on social media can manifest destiny.
The world does not mind spirituality.
Paul’s testimony in Acts 26 was not theoretical theology.
A violent collision between darkness and divine mercy.
Paul was once Saul of Tarsus.
A religious extremist convinced he was serving God.
In Philippians 3:5–6, Paul described himself as a Hebrew of Hebrews, a Pharisee, zealous for the law.
“At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun…”
ὑπὲρ τὴν λαμπρότητα τοῦ ἡλίου (hyper tēn lamprotēta tou hēliou)
“Beyond the brilliance of the sun itself.”
Most scholars believe this likely refers to Aramaic, the common Semitic language spoken by Jews in Judea during that period.
In Hebrew thought, repetition of a name carried emotional weight.
Jesus was confronting the man destroying Christians… while still pursuing him in mercy.
And this is where the Gospel becomes offensive to proud hearts.
Because grace destroys the illusion that we can save ourselves.
Paul did not evolve into righteousness.
Some of you reading this know exactly what that feels like.
The nights you smiled publicly while privately collapsing.
That kind of transformation confuses people.
Because the world understands behavior modification.
The Greek word Jesus used in John 3 for “born again” is:
It is resurrection life entering spiritually dead people.
That is why Paul could stand before rulers without fear.
Because he was no longer living for earthly approval.
And this is what unsettled Festus most.
The kind that only comes from someone who has truly encountered Christ.
“No sane man would suffer like this for a lie.”
But history proved Paul was telling the truth.
Because liars do not willingly embrace chains, beatings, shipwrecks, imprisonment, and execution for something they know is false.
His endurance revealed that Jesus was not merely an idea to him.
And deep down, many people still resist Christianity for the same reason Festus did.
Because if Jesus truly rose from the dead… then everything changes.
If the resurrection happened, then sin is real.
And suddenly life is no longer about comfort.
That is why the cross offends human pride.
“For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness…”
From where we derive the concept of moronic thinking.
To unbelieving minds, the Gospel sounds absurd.
An eternal kingdom invisible to earthly eyes.
“…but unto us which are saved it is the power of God.”
And maybe some people reading this have secretly been afraid of fully surrendering to Jesus because you fear what others will think.
The same world that called Paul insane now studies his writings two thousand years later.
The same Roman Empire that mocked Christianity collapsed.
But Jesus Christ is still saving souls.
Still raising spiritually dead people into new life.
Festus heard the Gospel and saw madness.
King Agrippa heard the Gospel and felt conviction.
“Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.”
And every person reading this will eventually respond one way or another.
Because nobody encounters the real Gospel neutrally.
C.S. Lewis famously argued that Christ could not merely be considered a good moral teacher if His claims were true. The testimony of Scripture presents Him as Lord, not merely inspiration.
The resurrection stands at the center of Christianity.
If Christ did not rise, Paul himself said our faith is vain.
But if He did rise… then ignoring Him becomes the greatest tragedy imaginable.
And maybe that is the hidden fear beneath Festus’ outburst.
Because sometimes people call truth insanity when truth threatens the life they want to keep living.
Conviction can sound offensive when darkness has become comfortable.
Some of you reading this have been fighting conviction for months.
You feel God calling you deeper.
But surrender feels terrifying because it changes everything.
Yet this is the beauty of the Gospel:
Jesus does not expose sin to destroy you.
He exposes sin to save you.
The cross was never proof that God hates sinners.
The cross is proof that God loves sinners enough to pay their debt Himself.
“But he was wounded for our transgressions…”
Christ was crushed beneath the weight of human rebellion.
And infinitely merciful toward sinners willing to repent.
That is why Paul could never stop preaching Jesus.
Because once you truly understand what Christ saved you from… silence becomes impossible.
Some people thought Paul was insane.
But maybe the real insanity is rejecting eternal life while obsessing over temporary things.
Maybe the real insanity is gaining worldly success while losing your soul.
Maybe the real insanity is pretending sin has no consequences.
Maybe the real insanity is spending your entire life avoiding the very God your heart was created for.
And awakened people unsettle sleeping worlds.
So if this exposed something hidden in your spirit… stop running.
Jesus Christ is still calling people out of darkness.
Still healing what religion could never heal.
Some people are one encounter away from complete transformation.
One day the voices that mocked your faith will stand before the same risen Christ they once rejected.
Bakit Inakala ni Festus na Baliw si Pablo
May mga eksena sa Bibliya na parang hindi lang basta mababasa.
Parang maririnig mo ang bigat ng katahimikan.
Parang mararamdaman mo ang tensyon sa hangin.
Ang Gawa 26 ay isa sa mga sandaling iyon.
Isang lalaking nakakadena ang nakatayo sa harap ng mga gobernador, sundalo, pinuno, relihiyosong lider, at hari.
At habang nagsasalita si Pablo… unti-unting nagiging hindi komportable ang buong silid.
Kundi dahil ang sinasabi niya ay imposible para sa isip ng tao.
Nagsasalita siya tungkol sa isang lalaking namatay… pero muling nabuhay.
Nagsasalita siya tungkol sa liwanag mula sa langit.
Isang tinig mula sa walang hanggan.
Isang Mesiyas na ipinako sa krus ngunit buhay.
Iyon talaga ang diwa ng sinabi niya sa Gawa 26:24.
Ang salitang μαίνῃ (mainē) ay galing sa salitang μαίνομαι (mainomai), na nangangahulugang:
• mawalan ng katinuan • parang wala sa sarili • magwala na parang nababaliw • magsalita na tila nasisiraan ng isip
Hindi simpleng hindi pagsang-ayon ang ginawa ni Festus.
Para sa kanya… nawalan na ng bait si Pablo.
At kung tutuusin, sa pananaw ng Roma, parang imposible nga ang mga sinasabi ni Pablo.
Dahil ang Ebanghelyo ay palaging mukhang kahangalan sa mga taong sumasamba sa kapangyarihan, kayamanan, kontrol, pride, at makamundong sistema.
At hanggang ngayon… ganoon pa rin.
Kapag sinabi mong binago ka ni Jesus, may mga taong nagiging hindi komportable.
Dahil ayaw ng mundo sa tunay na pagsuko kay Jesus.
Ayaw ng tao sa ideya na may Hari na mas mataas kaysa sarili nilang kagustuhan.
At iyon ang dahilan kung bakit parang baliw si Pablo sa mata ni Festus.
Habang ang lahat ay takot mawalan ng posisyon… si Pablo ay may kakaibang kapayapaan kahit nakakadena.
Habang ang lahat ay protektado ng kapangyarihan ng Roma… si Pablo ay nakatayo lang dala ang katotohanan.
At iyon ang hindi maintindihan ni Festus.
Paano nagkakaroon ng ganoong katapang ang isang taong posibleng ipapatay?
Dahil si Pablo ay hindi na nabubuhay para sa approval ng tao.
Dati siyang si Saul ng Tarsus.
Akala niya naglilingkod siya sa Diyos.
Pero sa daan papuntang Damascus… binasag ng langit ang kanyang kayabangan.
“Nakita ko ang isang liwanag mula sa langit na higit pa sa ningning ng araw.”
ὑπὲρ τὴν λαμπρότητα τοῦ ἡλίου (hyper tēn lamprotēta tou hēliou)
“Higit pa sa mismong liwanag ng araw.”
At pagkatapos ay nagsalita si Jesus.
Napakaganda ng detalye sa talatang iyon.
Sinasabi ng Kasulatan na nagsalita si Jesus sa “wikang Hebreo.”
Karamihan sa mga iskolar ay naniniwalang Aramaic ito — ang karaniwang wikang ginagamit noon ng mga Hudyo.
ay may malalim na emosyon sa kultura ng Hebreo.
Habang inuusig ni Saul ang mga Kristiyano… hinahabol pa rin siya ng awa ni Jesus.
At dito natitisod ang pride ng tao.
Dahil ipinapakita ng grasya na hindi natin kayang iligtas ang sarili natin.
Binagsak siya ng katotohanan hanggang siya ay sumuko.
At maraming tao ang makaka-relate dito.
May mga gabi kang umiiyak nang walang nakakaalam.
May mga kasalanang itinago mo nang matagal.
At pagkatapos… nakilala mo si Jesus.
Iyan ang hindi maintindihan ng mundo.
Pero hindi nila maintindihan ang spiritual rebirth.
Sa Juan 3, sinabi ni Jesus ang salitang:
Ang Kristiyanismo ay hindi simpleng pagiging mabuting tao.
Ito ay bagong buhay mula sa Diyos.
Kaya si Pablo ay nakatayo nang walang takot.
At minsan… ang katotohanan ang pinaka-nakakatakot pakinggan.
Lalo na kapag alam mong babaguhin nito ang buhay mo.
Maraming tao hanggang ngayon ang tumatakbo sa conviction.
Ayaw nilang sumuko kay Jesus dahil natatakot silang may kailangang bitawan.
Pero ang kagandahan ng Ebanghelyo ay ito:
Hindi inilalantad ni Jesus ang kasalanan para sirain ka.
Inilalantad Niya ito para iligtas ka.
Ang krus ay hindi patunay na galit ang Diyos sa makasalanan.
Patunay ito na mahal Niya tayo nang sapat para akuin Niya mismo ang parusa.
“Siya ay nasugatan dahil sa ating mga pagsalangsang…”
Ang Hebrew word para sa “nasugatan” ay:
At dahil doon… may pag-asa pa tayo.
Kaya hindi tumigil si Pablo sa pangangaral.
Kapag tunay mong naintindihan kung saan ka iniligtas ni Cristo… hindi ka na makakatahimik.
At baka iyon talaga ang dahilan kung bakit sinabi ni Festus na baliw si Pablo.
Dahil ang mga taong tunay na nabuhay para kay Jesus ay hindi na kayang kontrolin ng mundong ito.
At ang mga gising… palaging istorbo sa mundong tulog.
Kung may tinamaan sa puso mo habang binabasa ito… huwag mo nang takbuhan ang conviction.
Tinatawag ka pa rin ni Jesus.
May mga taong isang encounter na lang kay Jesus ang layo mula sa total transformation.
Darating ang araw na ang mundong tumawa sa pananampalataya mo ay haharap din sa parehong nabuhay na Cristo.
